page_metadata.title: Adapting existing toxicokinetic models to relate perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl intake to biomarkers in humans

model_classification.evidence_quote: Mean (95% CI) TK parameters for PFOS and PFOA fit to nonhuman primate data and scaled to humans.

model_context.stated_purpose: To facilitate reverse dosimetry and risk assessment for the less studied PFAS compounds in food, we developed and evaluated an approach to adapt existing toxicokinetic models for nonhuman primates to predict human serum levels.
model_context.current_application: human reverse dosimetry and risk assessment for PFAS compounds
model_context.source_quote: To facilitate reverse dosimetry and risk assessment for the less studied PFAS compounds in food, we developed and evaluated an approach to adapt existing toxicokinetic models for nonhuman primates to predict human serum levels.

adme_determinant_evidence.description: Saturable reabsorption from filtrate to central compartment via Michaelis-Menten kinetics
adme_determinant_evidence.evidence_quote: where a saturable process with a Michaelis–Menten kinetics dictates reabsorption from the filtrate compartment to the central compartment

adme_determinant_evidence.description: Free fraction in serum (Free) is highly correlated to resorption parameters Tmc and Kt
adme_determinant_evidence.evidence_quote: The Free parameter was found to be highly correlated to the resorption parameters; changing Free will then result in a change in Tmc and K t .
adme_determinant_evidence.source_location: Model parameters estimated for humans for both PFOA and PFOS

stated_assumptions.description: Saturable reabsorption from filtrate to central compartment follows Michaelis-Menten kinetics
stated_assumptions.evidence_quote: where a saturable process with a Michaelis–Menten kinetics dictates reabsorption from the filtrate compartment to the central compartment

stated_assumptions.description: Oral bioavailability initially set at 90% for both PFOS and PFOA to reflect high fraction of administered dose reaching systemic circulation after oral ingestion
stated_assumptions.evidence_quote: The bioavailability was initially set at 90% for both compounds to reflect a high fraction of an administered dose reaching systemic circulation after oral ingestion

stated_assumptions.description: TK model does not include a development compartment and thus underestimates serum levels in children and young adults by excluding gestation and breastfeeding exposures
stated_assumptions.evidence_quote: Data for individuals <20 years of age were excluded from the fitting process because the TK model does not include a development compartment and thus underestimates serum levels in children and young adults by excluding gestation and breastfeeding exposures.

stated_assumptions.description: Lower bioavailability observed in nonhuman primate model for PFOA assumed to be result of experiment-specific conditions
stated_assumptions.evidence_quote: the lower bioavailability observed in the nonhuman primate model was assumed to be the result of experiment-specific conditions
stated_assumptions.source_location: Model parameters estimated for humans for both PFOA and PFOS

stated_assumptions.description: Remaining parameters held constant between animal and human models except PFOA bioAv and Kt
stated_assumptions.evidence_quote: The remaining parameters were held constant between the animal and human models, as shown in Table 1 , with the exception of the PFOA bioAv and K t parameters, which were refit to the nonhuman primate data assuming a bioavailability of 90% for application in the human model
stated_assumptions.source_location: Model parameters estimated for humans for both PFOA and PFOS

stated_assumptions.evidence_quote: The Free parameters in these models were selected based on protein binding assay findings

stated_assumptions.evidence_quote: However, the binding efficacy may be higher in vitro than in vivo.

assumption_evidence.stated_assumption: TK model does not include a development compartment
assumption_evidence.authors_justification: Model underestimates serum levels in children and young adults by excluding gestation and breastfeeding exposures
assumption_evidence.structural_impact: Individuals <20 years of age excluded from fitting process; model applicable only to adults over 20
assumption_evidence.evidence_quote: Data for individuals <20 years of age were excluded from the fitting process because the TK model does not include a development compartment and thus underestimates serum levels in children and young adults by excluding gestation and breastfeeding exposures.

assumption_evidence.stated_assumption: Free fraction in serum selected from protein binding assay findings
assumption_evidence.authors_justification: Availability of compound-specific Free values for multiple PFAS compounds of interest
assumption_evidence.structural_impact: Free parameter highly correlated to resorption parameters Tmc and Kt; changing Free changes Tmc and Kt
assumption_evidence.source_location: Discussion; Model parameters estimated for humans for both PFOA and PFOS
assumption_evidence.evidence_quote: The Free parameters in these models were selected based on protein binding assay findings . An advantage of this approach is the availability of compound-specific Free values for multiple PFAS compounds of interest. However, the binding efficacy may be higher in vitro than in vivo.

assumption_evidence.stated_assumption: Lower bioavailability observed in nonhuman primate model for PFOA assumed to be result of experiment-specific conditions
assumption_evidence.authors_justification: Assumption that experimental conditions in nonhuman primate study do not reflect true human bioavailability
assumption_evidence.structural_impact: PFOA bioAv refit to nonhuman primate data assuming 90% bioavailability for human model application
assumption_evidence.source_location: Model parameters estimated for humans for both PFOA and PFOS
assumption_evidence.evidence_quote: the lower bioavailability observed in the nonhuman primate model was assumed to be the result of experiment-specific conditions

assumption_evidence.stated_assumption: Saturable resorption process likely minimal relevance for PFBS due to short half-life
assumption_evidence.evidence_quote: Given the short half-life of PFBS (<7 days) and the likely minimal relevance of the saturable resorption process, we decided not to pursue the study of this compound further.

items.details: The study explicitly distinguishes calibration (fitting to nonhuman primate data) from validation (simulating NHANES biomonitoring data and comparing PODHEDs to EPA models).

structured_details.training_comparison: Fitted to nonhuman primate serum data (PFOS, PFOA, PFHxS) using MCMC; predictions within factor of 2 for 98% (PFOS), 71% (PFOA), and 86% (PFHxS) of data points.
structured_details.validation_comparison: Validated against NHANES biomonitoring data (1999-2018) and compared PODHEDs to EPA-modified Verner model.
structured_details.observations: Observed serum levels from NHANES surveys and nonhuman primate studies.
structured_details.predictions: Predicted serum concentrations from the adapted human models and PODHEDs.
structured_details.limitations: NHANES validation excluded individuals <20 and >=80 years; model does not account for pregnancy/lactation.

evidence.source_quote: For the human models specifically, the performance of the resulting models was assessed by (i) simulating biomonitoring data in the NHANES
For PFOS, the model predictions were within a factor of 2 of the observed serum levels for 98% of the data points
Mean parameter estimates for the human PFOS and PFOA models were used to simulate NHANES biomonitoring data.

metrics: Percentage of data points within factor of 2
structured_details.criteria: Predictions within a factor of 2 of experimental data considered adequate; MSLE values reported for animal and human models.
structured_details.visual_assessment: Visual comparison of observed vs. predicted serum concentrations (log10 plots with ± one-half log10 dashed lines).
structured_details.applicability: Applicable for reverse dosimetry and risk assessment for PFAS compounds with limited human data; validated for PFOS, PFOA, and PFHxS.
structured_details.limitations: Model does not include development compartment (excludes gestation/lactation); NHANES validation limited to ages 21-79; differences in PODHEDs compared to EPA models due to clearance rate assumptions.

evidence.source_quote: Model performance was evaluated with mean square log errors (MSLE) and by visually comparing the commonalities between the observed and predicted data.
Predictions that were on average within a factor of 2 of the experimental data were considered adequate
The MSLE for the PFOS and PFOA models were 0.07 and 0.58, respectively
The inclusion of a development compartment to model gestational and lactational exposure to infants is a noted area for future improvement

items.question: Summarize influential parameters and the overall impact of sensitivity, variability, and uncertainty on outputs and reliability.
items.routing_rule: Use explicit reported results; do not infer reliability from parameter magnitude.
items.details: Free and bioavailability are highly influential; ka, k12, k21 have minimal impact. MCMC credible intervals quantify uncertainty; variability/uncertainty inclusion improves biomonitoring fit.

structured_details.overall_impact: Free and bioAv strongly influence resorption parameters and serum entry; ka/k12/k21 have minimal impact (<10% change in key parameters).
structured_details.reliability: Inference process robust for identifiable parameters; including variability/uncertainty captures more observed biomonitoring data.

evidence.source_quote: although some parameters (k12, k21, ka) were found to have a minimal impact on model outputs for the tested values... the values for Free and bioavailability for each compound were found to have a strong influence on results.
Notably, including variability and uncertainty in the parameter estimates for simulating the biomonitoring data would capture even more of the observed data
